title: Shared-bucket starvation: allocator regression causing batch underfill and fairness inversion
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2026-02-27 a capacity event exposed a regression in the batch allocator that resulted in sustained batch underfill, large tail latency spikes (p95->p99.9 delta of ~420ms for text-gen workloads), and fairness inversion across customers sharing a GPU pool. This ticket captures the incident findings, immediate mitigations, and a prioritized set of action items to prevent recurrence.

What happened: A change to the batch bucket allocator heuristic (deployed 2026-02-20 as part of runtime-1.29) introduced a soft-affinity optimization to prefer buckets with recent hot-prefixes. Under mixed traffic (many short, low-token requests + a subset of long-streaming requests) the allocator started concentrating requests into a small subset of buckets. Two effects followed: (1) bucket fragmentation and lock contention led to windowing stalls for under-utilized buckets; (2) the allocator's exponential backoff on contested buckets increased per-request queuing time, which starved other logical cohorts that were previously balanced by round-robin. The result: some requests never reached fill thresholds and were dispatched as tiny batches, decreasing throughput and increasing per-token cost for impacted customers while causing tail latency spikes for high-priority traffic.

Detection & scope: Alerting fired from the batch-formation SLO monitor when median batch size dropped by 35% and p99 latency rose above threshold. Affected pools: gpu-pool-eu-west-2 (three node clusters) and two dedicated customer pools. Customer impact: medium-high (billing increase for some tenants, degraded experience for a small set of enterprise customers).

Root cause: The new heuristic introduced two regressions in combination: (a) deterministic bucket affinity that reduced uniform distribution across buckets under adversarial request mixes; (b) a lock acquisition policy that used backoff windows proportional to contention, causing prioritized cohorts to hold effective monopoly of available slots for sustained intervals. A unit test gap allowed the deterministic affinity behavior to go untested under realistic interleaved workloads.

Immediate mitigation applied during incident: 1) Rolled back the allocator heuristic feature flag (runtime-1.29 -> rollback to runtime-1.28 behavior) which restored round-robin distribution. 2) Temporarily increased bucket pool size by +50% in affected clusters. 3) Flipped a per-pool emergency config to cap backoff at 5ms for contested acquisitions. These changes recovered batch fill and reduced tail latency within 18 minutes.

Longer-term fixes proposed (prioritized):
- Fix A (P0): Rework allocator to use probabilistic weighted distribution with contention-aware counters instead of deterministic hot-affinity. Add microbenchmarks and synthetic interleaved workload tests. Owner: Lars Holm. Estimate: 5 points.
- Fix B (P0): Replace exponential backoff with capped randomized backoff and integrate lock-free fast-path for uncontested allocations. Owner: Mei Chen. Estimate: 3 points.
- Fix C (P1): Add a clustering test harness that simulates mixed short/long request workloads and measures batch-size distribution and fairness metrics across 1000 simulated keys. Owner: Samuel Ortiz. Estimate: 5 points.
- Fix D (P1): Add telemetry: per-bucket acquisition time histogram, per-cohort fill-rate, and per-node allocator-pressure metric. Dashboard and alerts. Owner: Observability team (Emily Nguyen). Estimate: 3 points.
- Fix E (P2): Update runbook with emergency flags, quick rollback steps, and a new diagnostic play that captures bucket histograms on demand. Owner: SRE (Ravi Kaur). Estimate: 2 points.

Testing & rollout plan:
- Validate reworked allocator via unit tests + integration harness (internal CI), then deploy to canary pool for 48h with synthetic mixed traffic at 2x baseline.
- Gate using: stable batch fill metric (>=95% baseline) and no >10% p99 increase on canary.
- Progressive rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback if p99 degradation triggers.

Open questions & trade-offs noted:
- Probabilistic allocation avoids strict affinity but may slightly increase cache churn (KV cache). We need to measure token-cache hit rate impact during canary.
- Capping backoff reduces worst-case stall but may increase retry noise; will couple with rate-limiting suggestions for noisy tenants.

Acceptance criteria for this ticket (must be met before close):
1) Allocator redesign merged and green tests in CI, plus integration harness reports no fairness regression.
2) Observability dashboards added and at least two meaningful alerts configured.
3) Runbook updated with rollback and diagnostic steps.
4) Canary rollout executed with no customer-facing regressions and sign-off from owner + PM.

Customer impact: medium
